intent.text:
Motion (seat ses), on q1: Remove Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) from the global ~/.claude/settings.json now. Re-add it only in project or local settings for the repo that needs CC_AGENT, and only after the adversarial tests pass in the live harness: the export followed by `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, a newline, a backtick, and an injection inside the quoted value, each showing a prompt; plus one run with a second PreToolUse hook that also rewrites Bash, confirming the string the permission check sees.

On rec's point that removal makes attribution silent: I think the failure is not silent. Without the rule, the export prompts the agent, so the gap shows up at the moment it happens. A missing prefix that the agent sees and can report is better than an allow that admits unseen commands in every session. I accept rec's condition that vsect or the record should verify the CC_AGENT value that actually ran, and I accept sec's point that the rule should not be the only identity check. Those can land in parallel with the test work.

I would vote for this motion and would revisit keeping the rule globally only if the tests pass and the scope is narrowed.
